items.prompt: A student claims: 'The English word "sugar" comes from Arabic صفر (ṣifr).' Correct this statement, since ṣifr actually gives us a different English word. Which word did صفر (ṣifr) actually give English, and what does ṣifr mean in Arabic?

items.prompt: Why do many Arabic letters look different depending on whether they appear at the beginning, middle, or end of a word? Answer in one sentence.
items.answer: Because most Arabic letters change shape to connect with neighboring letters depending on their position (initial, medial, final, or isolated) in a word.

items.answer: Isolated (standalone), initial, medial, and final forms.

items.answer: non-connecting (letters that only connect on the right side, not the left)

items.answer: This is false — م (mīm) changes shape depending on position: isolated (م), initial (مـ), medial (ـمـ), and final (ـم).

items.prompt: What is the general purpose of a 'transliteration' or 'transcription' system, as used for Arabic in this book?
items.answer: It represents the sounds of Arabic words using Latin letters, so learners can read pronunciation without yet knowing Arabic script.

items.prompt: In common transliteration systems, a straight apostrophe (') or the symbol ء is used to represent which Arabic consonant sound, which is a brief closing of the throat?
items.answer: The hamza (glottal stop) sound.

items.prompt: In transliteration, the symbol ʻ (a reversed apostrophe, sometimes written as '3' informally) usually stands for which distinct Arabic letter?
items.answer: ع (ʻayn), a voiced pharyngeal sound with no English equivalent.

items.prompt: A learner transliterates the Arabic word سلام (peace) as 'salam' with no long vowel marked. Correct the transliteration to properly show vowel length.

items.prompt: Why do different textbooks and websites sometimes use different transliteration symbols for the same Arabic letter (for example ḥ vs. 7 for ح)?
items.answer: Because there is no single official standard; transliteration is only an approximate reading aid, so authors choose their own conventions to represent Arabic sounds that have no exact English letter equivalent.

items.prompt: The Arabic letter ب (bāʼ) changes shape depending on its position in a word. Name the four positional forms it can take (e.g., 'isolated, initial, medial, final') and briefly describe how the tooth/dot shape differs between isolated and medial position.
items.answer: The four forms are: isolated (ب), initial (بـ), medial (ـبـ), final (ـب). In isolated form the letter has a full tooth-like curve with the dot underneath and stands alone. In medial form the curve becomes a small connecting stroke joined to both the previous and following letters, with the dot still underneath, but the shape is flatter/shorter since it connects on both sides.

items.prompt: Complete the sentence: Arabic is written and read from ___ to ___ (give the direction in English).
items.answer: right to left

items.prompt: A student transliterated the Arabic letter خ (khāʼ) as 'k' in Latin script. Explain why this is incorrect and give the correct transliteration convention used for خ (as commonly written in Romanization, e.g., in this course).
items.answer: خ is a distinct sound (a voiceless uvular/velar fricative, like the 'ch' in Scottish 'loch'), different from ك (kāf, plain 'k'). The correct transliteration is 'kh', not 'k', to distinguish it from ك.

items.prompt: Name two Arabic letters that are never connected to the letter following them (i.e., they only connect to the letter before them, not after), and explain what effect this has on the word's shape.
items.answer: Examples include د (dāl), ذ (dhāl), ر (rāʼ), ز (zāy), و (wāw), and ا (alif). Because these letters don't connect forward, the next letter in the word must start a new isolated or initial form, creating a visible break in the connected script within the word.

items.prompt: Translate into English: the Arabic letter name "عين" (ʿayn).
items.answer: The letter 'ayn (a voiced pharyngeal fricative with no equivalent sound in English, often transliterated with the symbol ʿ)

items.prompt: Fill in the blank: In the Latin transliteration system used for Arabic, a straight apostrophe-like symbol (ء or ʼ) is used to represent the sound called the ___ , a brief catch in the throat similar to the sound in the middle of 'uh-oh'.
items.answer: hamza (glottal stop)

items.prompt: Explain why the same English letter 's' might be used to transliterate two different Arabic letters, س (sīn) and ص (ṣād). What symbol is typically added to distinguish ص from س in careful transliteration?
items.answer: Both س and ص sound similar to an English 's', but ص is a 'heavier' or emphatic (pharyngealized) version of the sound. To distinguish them, careful transliteration adds a dot beneath the letter: ṣ for ص, while س remains plain s.

items.prompt: A learner wrote the word for 'house' as connecting the letters ب - ي - ت (b-y-t) but drew the ي (yāʼ) in its isolated form even though it appears in the middle of the word. What is wrong with this, and how should the medial form of ي differ from its isolated form?
items.answer: The error is using the isolated form of ي in a medial position; since ي connects on both sides, it must use its medial form. The isolated form of ي has a full curved tail with two dots underneath, while the medial form is a smaller connecting stroke without the tail, keeping the two dots underneath, joined smoothly to the letters before and after it.

items.prompt: The verb ذهب (dhahaba, 'he went') is an irregular (hollow) verb because of its middle weak letter. In your own words, briefly explain what makes a verb 'irregular/weak' in Arabic and why it can change spelling in conjugation.
items.answer: A weak (irregular) verb contains a weak letter (و, ي, or أ) as one of its three root letters, often in the middle or final position. During conjugation, this weak letter may shift, drop, or merge with vowels, causing spelling changes that don't follow the regular sound-verb pattern (e.g., ذهب → أذهب, يذهب stays fairly regular here, but hollow/defective verbs like قال or رأى show more dramatic shifts).

items.answer: 25 years old

items.prompt: Complete with the correct household item: أَنَا أَجْلِسُ عَلَى ___ فِي غُرْفَةِ الجُلُوسِ (ʾanā ʾajlisu ʿalā ___ fī ghurfat al-julūs) 'I sit on the ___ in the living room.'
items.answer: الكُرْسِيّ (al-kursī) 'chair' or الأَرِيكَة (al-ʾarīkah) 'sofa'

items.prompt: Find and fix the error: هُوَ تَعْمَلُ فِي المَكْتَبِ (huwa taʿmalu fī al-maktab) 'He works in the office.'
items.answer: هُوَ يَعْمَلُ فِي المَكْتَبِ (huwa yaʿmalu fī al-maktab) — the verb prefix should match masculine 'he' (يَـ ya-), not feminine (تَـ ta-)

items.prompt: Answer in a full Arabic sentence with transliteration: مَاذَا تَسْتَعْمِلُ لِلطَّبْخِ فِي المَطْبَخِ؟ (mādhā tastaʿmilu lil-ṭabkh fī al-maṭbakh?) 'What do you use for cooking in the kitchen?'

items.prompt: Fill in the correct possessive pronoun suffix: هَذَا كِتَابُ___ (hādhā kitābu___) 'This is my book.'
items.answer: هَذَا كِتَابِي (hādhā kitābī) — suffix ي (-ī) for 'my'

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic (with transliteration): 'I clean the house every day.'
items.answer: أُنَظِّفُ البَيْتَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ (ʾunaẕẕifu al-bayta kulla yawmin)

items.prompt: Complete with the correct word for 'desk': القلم على ال___ (al-qalam 'ala al-___) - 'The pen is on the desk.'
items.answer: مكتب (maktab)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'The computer is on the table.'
items.answer: الكمبيوتر على الطاولة (al-kombiyootar 'ala al-taawila)

items.prompt: Translate into English: البيت فيه مطبخ وغرفة نوم وحمام (al-bayt feehi matbakh wa-ghurfat nawm wa-hammaam)
items.answer: The house has a kitchen, a bedroom, and a bathroom.

items.answer: تكتبون (taktuboona)

items.prompt: Find and correct the error in gender agreement: الطاولة كبير (al-taawila kabeer) - meant to say 'the table is big.'
items.answer: الطاولة كبيرة (al-taawila kabeera) - 'kabeer' must become feminine 'kabeera' to agree with the feminine noun 'taawila'.

items.prompt: Name three household objects in Arabic (with transliteration) that you might find in a bedroom or kitchen.
items.answer: Example: سرير (sareer - bed), ثلاجة (thallaaja - refrigerator), كرسي (kursi - chair) - any three correct household nouns accepted.

items.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct present-tense form of يطبخ (yatbakhu - 'to cook'): أمي ___ الطعام كل يوم (ummi ___ al-ta'aam kull yawm) - 'My mother cooks food every day.'
items.answer: تطبخ (tatbakhu)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'I clean the kitchen every day.'
items.answer: أنظف المطبخ كل يوم (unazzifu al-matbakh kull yawm)

items.prompt: Correct the verb conjugation error: هم يعمل في المكتب (hum ya'malu fil-maktab) - meant to say 'they (masc. pl.) work in the office.'
items.answer: هم يعملون في المكتب (hum ya'maloona fil-maktab) - the verb must take the masculine plural ending '-oona'.

items.prompt: Write one full sentence in Arabic describing what you do at the office, using the verb يعمل (ya'malu) or another work-related verb.
items.answer: Example: أنا أعمل على الكمبيوتر في المكتب (ana a'malu 'ala al-kombiyootar fil-maktab) - 'I work on the computer in the office.' Any grammatically correct sentence with a work verb accepted.

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb يقرأ (yaqra'u - 'to read') in the present tense for نحن (nahnu - 'we').
items.answer: نقرأ (naqra'u)

items.prompt: Translate into English: مَا اسْمُكَ؟ (mā ismuka?)
items.answer: What is your name? (to a male)

items.prompt: Complete with the correct possessive suffix meaning 'my': هَذِهِ أُسْرَت___ (hādhihi usrat___) — 'This is my family.'
items.answer: ي (i) → أُسْرَتِي (usratī)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb يَعْمَلُ (ya'malu, 'to work') in the present tense for 'أَنَا' (anā, I) and 'هِيَ' (hiya, she).
items.answer: أَنَا أَعْمَلُ (anā a'malu) / هِيَ تَعْمَلُ (hiya ta'malu)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'I work as a teacher.'
items.answer: أَعْمَلُ مُعَلِّمًا (a'malu mu'alliman) — for a female speaker: أَعْمَلُ مُعَلِّمَةً (a'malu mu'allimatan)

items.prompt: Find and fix the error: عِنْدهُ أَخَوَات وَأَخ (ʿindhu akhawāt wa akh) — meant to say 'He has sisters and a brother.'
items.answer: عِنْدَهُ أَخَوَاتٌ وَأَخٌ (ʿindahu akhawātun wa akhun) — missing the short vowel 'a' on عِنْدَ and correct tanwīn endings

items.prompt: Answer in Arabic with a short sentence: كَمْ أَخًا وَأُخْتًا لَدَيْكَ؟ (kam akhan wa ukhtan ladayka? — 'How many brothers and sisters do you have?')
items.answer: Any grammatically correct sentence, e.g., لَدَيَّ أَخٌ وَأُخْتَانِ (ladayya akhun wa ukhtān) — 'I have one brother and two sisters.'

items.prompt: Complete the phone greeting: أَ-َلُو، مَنْ ___؟ (alū, man ___? — 'Hello, who is speaking?')
items.answer: يَتَكَلَّمُ (yatakallamu) → مَنْ يَتَكَلَّمُ؟ (man yatakallamu?)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'I will send you an email tomorrow.'
items.answer: سَأُرْسِلُ لَكَ رِسَالَةَ بَرِيدٍ إِلِكْتْرُونِيّ غَدًا (sa-ursilu laka risālata barīdin iliktrūnī ghadan)

items.prompt: Translate into English: من أنتَ؟ (man anta?)
items.answer: Who are you? (to a male)

items.answer: كم (kam)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'What is your job?' (to a man)
items.answer: ما هي مهنتك؟ (mā hiya mihnatuka?)

items.prompt: Fill in the missing family word: أخي و ...... يعيشان في القاهرة (akhī wa ______ ya'īshān fī al-Qāhira) — 'My brother and my sister live in Cairo.'
items.answer: أختي (ukhtī)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb يَعْمَلُ (ya'malu, 'to work') in the present tense for أنتِ (anti, 'you' fem. sing.)
items.answer: تَعْمَلينَ (ta'malīna)

items.answer: هل أنتِ طبيبة؟ (hal anti ṭabība?) — corrected spelling of أنتِ

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'I have three children.'
items.answer: لدي ثلاثة أولاد (ladayya thalāthat awlād)

items.prompt: Answer in Arabic with a full sentence: أين تعمل؟ (ayna ta'mal? — 'Where do you work?') Give any plausible answer.
items.answer: Any correct sentence, e.g. أعمل في مكتب (a'malu fī maktab) — 'I work in an office.'

items.prompt: Complete the phone phrase: ...... من فضلك (______ min faḍlik) — 'Hold on, please' (used when answering a call)
items.answer: لحظة (laḥẕa)

items.prompt: Translate into English: هل يمكنني ترك رسالة؟ (hal yumkinunī tark risāla?)
items.answer: Can I leave a message?

items.prompt: Correct the error: أرسلت لك بريد إلكتروني بالأمس مساءً (arsaltu laka barīd 'elektrōnī bi-l-amsi masā'an) — the verb tense should show past feminine agreement if 'I' is a woman speaking. Fix if the speaker is female and the verb form is wrong: أرسلت (arsaltu) should stay the same or change?
items.answer: أرسلتُ (arsaltu) is correct for both genders in first person; no change needed — this item highlights that first-person past tense doesn't change by gender.

items.prompt: Write one short sentence in Arabic asking a friend for their email address.
items.answer: Example: ما هو بريدك الإلكتروني؟ (mā huwa barīduka al-elektrōnī?) — 'What is your email address?'

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'Where is the bank?'
items.answer: أَيْنَ البَنْكُ؟ (ayna al-banku?)

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct imperative verb meaning 'go' (masculine singular command): اِذْهَبْ إلى المَطْعَمِ (___ ilā al-maṭ‘am) — 'Go to the restaurant.'
items.answer: اِذْهَبْ (idhhab)

items.prompt: Conjugate the imperative of the verb دَخَلَ (dakhala, 'to enter') for: 1) أَنْتَ (anta, you m.), 2) أَنْتِ (anti, you f.), 3) أَنْتُمْ (antum, you pl. m.)
items.answer: 1) اُدْخُلْ (udkhul) 2) اُدْخُلِي (udkhulī) 3) اُدْخُلُوا (udkhulū)

items.prompt: Translate into English: اِلتَفِتْ يَمِينًا عِنْدَ الإِشَارَةِ (iltafit yamīnan ‘inda al-ishārah)
items.answer: 'Turn right at the traffic light.'

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct ordinal number: هٰذَا هُوَ الشَّارِعُ ___ (hādhā huwa ash-shāri‘ ___) — 'This is the third street.' (شارع is masculine)
items.answer: الثّالِثُ (ath-thālith)

items.prompt: Find and correct the error in this command sentence: اِذْهَبِي مُبَاشَرَةً ثُمَّ يَسَار (idh-habī mubāsharatan thumma yasār) — meant to say 'Go straight, then turn left' (feminine command).
items.answer: Missing verb 'turn'; should be: اِذْهَبِي مُبَاشَرَةً ثُمَّ اِلْتَفِتِي يَسَارًا (idh-habī mubāsharatan thumma iltafitī yasāran)

items.prompt: Someone asks: أَيْنَ المَكْتَبَةُ؟ هَلْ هِيَ قَرِيبَةٌ مِنْ هُنَا؟ (ayna al-maktabah? hal hiya qarībah min hunā?) — What two things is the person asking?
items.answer: They are asking where the library is, and whether it is near here.

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'The second door is on the left, and the fourth door is on the right.'
items.answer: البَابُ الثّانِي عَلَى اليَسَارِ، والبَابُ الرّابِعُ عَلَى اليَمِينِ (al-bābu ath-thānī ‘alā al-yasār, wa-al-bābu ar-rābi‘ ‘alā al-yamīn)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'Where is the bank?'
items.answer: أَيْنَ البَنْكُ؟ (ayna al-bank?)

items.answer: دُرْ يَمِينًا (dur yamīnan) - 'Turn right!'

items.prompt: Give the imperative form of the verb ذَهَبَ (dhahaba, 'to go') for: (a) أَنْتَ (anta, 'you' masc. sing.) (b) أَنْتِ (anti, 'you' fem. sing.) (c) أَنْتُمْ (antum, 'you' masc. pl.)
items.answer: (a) اِذْهَبْ (idhhab) (b) اِذْهَبِي (idhhabī) (c) اِذْهَبُوا (idhhabū)

items.prompt: Find and fix the error in this command to a woman: اُكْتُبْ اسْمَكِ هُنَا (uktub ismaki hunā) - 'Write your name here.'
items.answer: Should be اُكْتُبِي اسْمَكِ هُنَا (uktubī ismaki hunā) - feminine imperative ending needs ي (ī), not the masculine form.

items.prompt: Complete the direction phrase: سِرْ إِلَى ____ (sir ilā ____) meaning 'Go straight ahead.'
items.answer: سِرْ إِلَى الأَمَامِ (sir ilā al-amām)

items.prompt: In Arabic, how do you say 'next to the mosque'? (give the phrase, using بِجَانِبِ or قُرْبَ)
items.answer: بِجَانِبِ المَسْجِدِ (bijānibi al-masjid) or قُرْبَ المَسْجِدِ (qurba al-masjid)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic (command to a group of men): 'Cross the street!'
items.answer: اُعْبُرُوا الشَّارِعَ! (u'burū ash-shāri'a!)

items.prompt: Complete the ordinal number: الشَّارِعُ ____ عَلَى اليَمِينِ (ash-shāri' ____ 'alā al-yamīn) meaning 'The third street on the right.'
items.answer: الشَّارِعُ الثَّالِثُ (ash-shāri' ath-thālith)

items.prompt: Translate into English: الطَّابِقُ الخَامِسُ (aT-Tābiq al-khāmis)
items.answer: The fifth floor

items.prompt: Give the negative imperative (command not to do something) for 'Don't turn left!' addressed to a man, using the verb دَارَ (dāra, 'to turn').
items.answer: لا تَدُرْ يَسَارًا! (lā tadur yasāran!)

items.prompt: Someone asks: كَيْفَ أَذْهَبُ إِلَى المَكْتَبَةِ؟ (kayfa adhhabu ilā al-maktaba?). Write a short direction reply in Arabic telling them to go straight, then turn left at the second street.
items.answer: Sample answer: سِرْ إِلَى الأَمَامِ ثُمَّ دُرْ يَسَارًا عِنْدَ الشَّارِعِ الثَّانِي (sir ilā al-amām thumma dur yasāran 'inda ash-shāri' ath-thānī) - 'Go straight then turn left at the second street.'

items.prompt: Complete the sentence: أنا أتناول (...) في الصباح باكراً. (ana atanāwalu (...) fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ bākiran) — 'I eat (...) early in the morning.' Fill in the Arabic word for 'breakfast'.
items.answer: فطور (fuṭūr / faṭūr) — 'أنا أتناول الفطور في الصباح باكراً.'

items.prompt: Translate into English: هل يمكنني أن أرى قائمة الطعام من فضلك؟ (hal yumkinunī an ara qāʾimat aṭ-ṭaʿām min faḍlik?)
items.answer: 'May I see the menu, please?'

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb طَلَبَ (ṭalaba, 'to order/request') in the present tense (المضارع) for: أنا (anā), أنتَ (anta), هي (hiya), نحن (naḥnu).
items.answer: أنا أطلب (anā aṭlubu); أنتَ تطلب (anta taṭlubu); هي تطلب (hiya taṭlubu); نحن نطلب (naḥnu naṭlubu)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'I would like a cup of tea and a piece of cake.'
items.answer: أريد كوب شاي وقطعة كعك. (urīdu kūb shāy wa-qiṭʿat kaʿk)

items.prompt: Find and correct the grammatical error: النادل تعطيني الفاتورة. (an-nādilu tuʿṭīnī al-fātūrah) — intended meaning: 'The waiter gives me the bill.'
items.answer: النادل يعطيني الفاتورة. (an-nādilu yuʿṭīnī al-fātūrah) — the verb must agree with the masculine subject النادل, so it should be يعطيني (yuʿṭīnī), not تعطيني (tuʿṭīnī).

items.prompt: Read this short exchange and answer in English: الزبون: الحساب من فضلك. النادل: بالطبع، المجموع خمسون ريالاً. هل تدفع نقداً أم بالبطاقة؟ الزبون: بالبطاقة. (az-zabūn: al-ḥisāb min faḍlik. an-nādil: bi-ṭ-ṭabʿ, al-majmūʿ khamsūn riyālan. hal tadfaʿ naqdan am bi-l-biṭāqah? az-zabūn: bi-l-biṭāqah.) Question: How is the customer paying, and how much is the total?
items.answer: The customer is paying by card (بالبطاقة / bi-l-biṭāqah), and the total is fifty riyals (خمسون ريالاً / khamsūn riyālan).

items.prompt: Complete with the correct preposition: نأكل الغداء (...) الساعة الواحدة ظهراً. (naʾkulu al-ghadāʾ (...) as-sāʿah al-wāḥidah ẓuhran) — 'We eat lunch at one o'clock in the afternoon.'
items.answer: في (fī) — 'نأكل الغداء في الساعة الواحدة ظهراً.'

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'The food is delicious, but the bill is expensive.'
items.answer: الطعام لذيذ، لكن الفاتورة غالية. (aṭ-ṭaʿām ladhīdh, lākin al-fātūrah ghāliyah)

items.prompt: Translate to English: الفَطور (al-faṭūr)
items.answer: breakfast

items.prompt: Translate to Arabic (with transliteration): 'dinner'
items.answer: العَشاء (al-‘ashā’)

items.prompt: Complete the sentence: أريدُ أن أطلبَ ______ (urīdu an aṭluba ______) meaning 'I want to order a cup of tea.'
items.answer: كوبَ شاي (kūba shāy)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb أَكَلَ (akala, 'to eat') in the present tense (المضارع) for 'هو' (huwa, he) and 'هي' (hiya, she).
items.answer: هو يأكل (huwa ya’kulu) — he eats; هي تأكل (hiya ta’kulu) — she eats

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb شَرِبَ (shariba, 'to drink') in the present tense for 'أنا' (anā, I) and 'نحن' (naḥnu, we).
items.answer: أنا أشرب (anā ashrabu) — I drink; نحن نشرب (naḥnu nashrabu) — we drink

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic (give transliteration too): 'Can I have the menu, please?'
items.answer: هل يمكنني أن أرى قائمةَ الطعام، من فضلك؟ (hal yumkinunī an arā qā’imata aṭ-ṭa‘āmi, min faḍlik?)

items.prompt: Read: النادل قال: 'ماذا تريد أن تشرب؟' فقالت الزبونة: 'أريد عصير برتقال، من فضلك.' (an-nādil qāla: 'mādhā turīdu an tashrab?' fa-qālat az-zabūnah: 'urīdu ‘aṣīr burtuqāl, min faḍlik.') Question: What did the customer order to drink?
items.answer: Orange juice (عصير برتقال / ‘aṣīr burtuqāl)

items.prompt: Find and fix the mistake: أنا يأكل الخبز كل صباح (anā ya’kulu al-khubz kulla ṣabāḥ) — 'I eat bread every morning.'
items.answer: أنا آكل الخبز كل صباح (anā ākulu al-khubz kulla ṣabāḥ) — the verb must agree with 'أنا' (I), so it should be آكل (ākulu), not يأكل (ya’kulu).

items.prompt: Complete: عندما ننتهي من الأكل، نطلب من النادل ______ (‘indamā nantahī min al-akl, naṭlubu min an-nādil ______) meaning 'the bill/check.'
items.answer: الحساب (al-ḥisāb)

items.prompt: Translate into English: هل الحساب يشمل الخدمة؟ (hal al-ḥisāb yashmulu al-khidmah?)
items.answer: Does the bill include the service (tip)?

items.prompt: In Arabic, write one full sentence asking a waiter for a table for two people. (Give transliteration.)
items.answer: Example: هل يمكن أن نحصل على طاولة لشخصين؟ (hal yumkin an naḥṣula ‘alā ṭāwilah li-shakhṣayn?) — 'Can we get a table for two?'

items.prompt: Find and fix the mistake: الزبون يأكل في المطبخ لأنه لا يجد طاولة. (az-zabūn ya’kulu fī al-maṭbakh li-annahu lā yajidu ṭāwilah) — 'The customer eats in the kitchen because he can't find a table.' (Wrong word for the dining area is used.)
items.answer: الزبون يأكل في المطعم لأنه لا يجد طاولة. (az-zabūn ya’kulu fī al-maṭ‘am ...) — 'restaurant' (المطعم / al-maṭ‘am) is correct, not 'kitchen' (المطبخ / al-maṭbakh).

items.prompt: Write a short Arabic sentence (with transliteration) saying you would like to pay by credit card.
items.answer: Example: أريد أن أدفعَ ببطاقة الائتمان (urīdu an adfa‘a bi-biṭāqat al-i’timān) — 'I want to pay with a credit card.'

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'This shirt is expensive.' (use قَمِيص for shirt, غَالِي for expensive)
items.answer: هَذَا الْقَمِيصُ غَالِي (haadhaa al-qamiisu ghaalii)

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct comparative form of رخيص (rakhiis, cheap): هَذَا الْحِذَاءُ ____ مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْحِذَاءِ (haadhaa al-hidhaa'u ____ min dhaalika al-hidhaa'i) — 'This shoe is cheaper than that shoe.'
items.answer: أَرْخَص (arkhas)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb اِشْتَرَى (ishtaraa, 'to buy') in the past tense for 'she' (هِيَ, hiya) and 'they' (هُمْ, hum).
items.answer: هِيَ اِشْتَرَتْ (hiya ishtarat) — she bought; هُمْ اِشْتَرَوْا (hum ishtarau) — they bought

items.prompt: In a clothing store, how would you ask a salesperson in Arabic: 'Do you have this in a bigger size?' (use حَجْم for size, أَكْبَر for bigger)
items.answer: هَلْ لَدَيْكَ هَذَا بِحَجْمٍ أَكْبَر؟ (hal ladayka haadhaa bi-hajmin akbar?)

items.prompt: Correct the grammatical error in this sentence: هَذَا الْبَيْت أَجْمَل مِن ذَلِك الْبَيْتِ الْكَبِير (haadhaa al-baytu ajmal min dhaalika al-baytu al-kabiir) — 'This house is more beautiful than that big house.'
items.answer: The word after مِن (min) must be in the genitive case (majrur), not nominative: ...مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْبَيْتِ الْكَبِيرِ (min dhaalika al-bayti al-kabiiri) — the final ت needs kasra (بَيْتِ), not damma (بَيْتُ)

items.prompt: Translate into English: كَمْ سِعْرُ هَذِهِ الْحَقِيبَةِ؟ (kam si'ru haadhihi al-haqiibati?)
items.answer: How much does this bag cost? / What is the price of this bag?

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the appropriate word for 'small' (as in clothing size) to complete: أُرِيدُ حَجْمًا ____ ، هَذَا كَبِيرٌ جِدًّا عَلَيَّ (uriidu hajman ____, haadhaa kabiirun jiddan 'alayya) — 'I want a small size, this is too big for me.'
items.answer: صَغِيرًا (saghiiran)

items.prompt: Write one short sentence in Arabic comparing the price of two items, using أَغْلَى (aghlaa, 'most expensive/more expensive'). For example, compare a watch (سَاعَة, saa'ah) and a ring (خَاتَم, khaatam).
items.answer: Example: السَّاعَةُ أَغْلَى مِنَ الْخَاتَمِ (al-saa'atu aghlaa mina al-khaatami) — 'The watch is more expensive than the ring.'

items.prompt: Translate to English: هَذَا الْقَمِيصُ رَخِيصٌ وَذَلِكَ غَالٍ (hādhā al-qamīṣu rakhīṣun wa-dhālika ghālin)
items.answer: This shirt is cheap and that one is expensive.

items.prompt: Complete with the comparative form of كَبِير (kabīr, 'big'): هَذَا الْمَقَاسُ ___ مِنْ ذَلِكَ (hādhā al-maqāsu ___ min dhālika) = 'This size is bigger than that one.'
items.answer: أَكْبَرُ (akbaru)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb اِشْتَرَى (ishtarā, 'to buy') in the past tense for هِيَ (hiya, 'she').
items.answer: اِشْتَرَتْ (ishtarat)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb بَاعَ (bāʿa, 'to sell') in the present tense for نَحْنُ (naḥnu, 'we').
items.answer: نَبِيعُ (nabīʿu)

items.prompt: Translate to Arabic: 'What is the price of this dress?'
items.answer: مَا ثَمَنُ هَذَا الْفُسْتَانِ؟ (mā thamanu hādhā al-fustāni?)

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct comparative: هَذَا الْحِذَاءُ ___ (jayyid, 'good') مِنَ الآخَرِ (min al-ākhar) = 'This shoe is better than the other.'
items.answer: أَجْوَدُ (ajwadu)

items.prompt: Find and correct the error: أَنَا يَشْتَرِي قَمِيصًا جَدِيدًا (anā yashtarī qamīṣan jadīdan) — intended meaning: 'I am buying a new shirt.'
items.answer: أَنَا أَشْتَرِي قَمِيصًا جَدِيدًا (anā ashtarī qamīṣan jadīdan) — the verb must agree with 'I' (أَنَا), so it should be أَشْتَرِي (ashtarī), not يَشْتَرِي (yashtarī).

items.prompt: In Arabic, write the word for 'size' (as in clothing size) and give its plural form.
items.answer: مَقَاس (maqās), plural: مَقَاسَات (maqāsāt)

items.prompt: Translate to Arabic: 'Do you have a smaller size?' (asking a male shopkeeper)
items.answer: هَلْ عِنْدَكَ مَقَاسٌ أَصْغَرُ؟ (hal ʿindaka maqāsun aṣgharu?)

items.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the verb لَبِسَ (labisa, 'to wear') for أَنْتِ (anti, 'you', feminine singular) in the present tense: أَنْتِ ___ فُسْتَانًا جَمِيلًا (anti ___ fustānan jamīlan) = 'You are wearing a beautiful dress.'
items.answer: تَلْبَسِينَ (talbasīna)

items.prompt: A shopkeeper says: هَذَا أَرْخَصُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَلَكِنَّهُ أَقَلُّ جَوْدَةً (hādhā arkhaṣu min dhālika wa-lākinnahu aqallu jawdatan). What is he telling the customer about the two items, in your own English words?
items.answer: He is saying this item is cheaper than that one, but it is of lower quality.

items.prompt: Translate to English: كُنْتُ أَبِيعُ الْمَلَابِسَ فِي هَذَا السُّوقِ (kuntu abīʿu al-malābisa fī hādhā as-sūqi)
items.answer: I used to sell clothes in this market.

items.prompt: Translate into English: كَمِ السَّاعَةُ الآن؟ (kam is-sā‘atu al-ān?)
items.answer: What time is it now?

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct Arabic word for 'half' to say 'It's 3:30' — السَّاعَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ و____ (as-sā‘atu ath-thālithatu wa____)
items.answer: نِصْف (niṣf)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb زَارَ (zāra, 'to visit') in the present tense (يَزُورُ - yazūru pattern) for 'we': نَحْنُ ____ المَسْجِدَ (naḥnu ____ al-masjida) 'We visit the mosque'
items.answer: نَزُورُ (nazūru)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'The museum is closed on Friday.'
items.answer: المَتْحَفُ مُغْلَقٌ يَوْمَ الجُمُعَةِ (al-mat-ḥafu mughlaqun yawma al-jum‘ah)

items.prompt: Correct the grammatical error in this sentence: أَنَا يَذْهَبُ إلى السِّينَما (anā yadh-habu ilā as-sīnamā) — intended meaning: 'I go to the cinema.'
items.answer: أَنَا أَذْهَبُ إلى السِّينَما (anā adh-habu ilā as-sīnamā) — the verb must match the first person 'I' (أَذْهَبُ), not the third person masculine (يَذْهَبُ).

items.prompt: In Arabic, write one full sentence answering: مَتَى تَذْهَبُ إلى المَسْجِدِ؟ (matā tadh-habu ilā al-masjid? 'When do you go to the mosque?') Use a time expression like يَوْمَ الجُمُعَةِ (yawm al-jum‘ah, 'on Friday') or فِي الصَّباحِ (fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ, 'in the morning').
items.answer: Any grammatically correct sentence such as: أَذْهَبُ إلى المَسْجِدِ يَوْمَ الجُمُعَةِ (adh-habu ilā al-masjidi yawma al-jum‘ah) — 'I go to the mosque on Friday.'

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the Arabic word for 'pilgrimage/Hajj': يَذْهَبُ المُسْلِمُونَ إلى مَكَّةَ لِأَداءِ ____ (yadh-habu al-muslimūna ilā makkata li-adā’i ____) 'Muslims go to Mecca to perform the ____.'
items.answer: الحَجّ (al-ḥajj)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'We are watching a film at eight o'clock in the evening.'
items.answer: نُشاهِدُ فِيلْمًا فِي السَّاعَةِ الثَّامِنَةِ مَساءً (nushāhidu fīlman fī as-sā‘ati ath-thāminati masā’an)

items.prompt: Translate into English: كَمِ السَّاعَةُ؟ (kam is-sāʿah?)
items.answer: What time is it?

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'It is three o'clock.'
items.answer: السَّاعَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ (is-sāʿah ath-thālithah)

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word for 'half': السَّاعَةُ الخَامِسَةُ وَ___ (is-sāʿah al-khāmisah wa___) = 'It is half past five.'
items.answer: نِصْف (niṣf)

items.prompt: Fill in the blank: أُحِبُّ زِيَارَةَ ___ لِأَنَّ فِيهِ آثَارًا قَدِيمَةً (uḥibbu ziyārata ___ li'anna fīhi āthāran qadīmah) — 'I like visiting the ___ because it has ancient artifacts.'
items.answer: المَتْحَف (al-matḥaf) - the museum

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb ذَهَبَ (dhahaba, 'to go') in the past tense for 'we': نَحْنُ ___ إِلَى السِّينَما (naḥnu ___ ilā s-sīnamā) — 'We went to the cinema.'
items.answer: ذَهَبْنَا (dhahabnā)

items.prompt: Correct the error in this sentence: هِيَ يَذْهَبُ إِلَى المَسْجِدِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ جُمْعَةٍ (hiya yadhhabu ilā l-masjidi kulla yawmi jumʿah) — 'She goes to the mosque every Friday.'
items.answer: هِيَ تَذْهَبُ إِلَى المَسْجِدِ كُلَّ يَوْمِ جُمْعَةٍ (hiya tadhhabu ilā l-masjidi kulla yawmi jumʿah) — verb must agree with feminine subject

items.prompt: In Arabic, name one thing a Muslim pilgrim does during الحَجّ (al-ḥajj, 'the Hajj') — write a short phrase in Arabic with transliteration.
items.answer: Example: الطَّوَافُ حَوْلَ الكَعْبَةِ (aṭ-ṭawāf ḥawla l-kaʿbah) — 'circling the Kaaba'

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'The film starts at seven o'clock.'
items.answer: يَبْدَأُ الفِيلْمُ السَّاعَةَ السَّابِعَةَ (yabda'u l-fīlmu s-sāʿata s-sābiʿah)

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: سَنَذْهَبُ ___ الكَنِيسَةِ يَوْمَ الأَحَدِ (sanadhhabu ___ l-kanīsati yawma l-aḥad) — 'We will go to the church on Sunday.'
items.answer: إِلَى (ilā)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb زَارَ (zāra, 'to visit') in the present tense for 'you (masc. singular)': أَنْتَ ___ المَتْحَفَ غَدًا (anta ___ l-matḥafa ghadan) — 'You will visit the museum tomorrow.'
items.answer: تَزُورُ (tazūru)

items.prompt: Write a short sentence in Arabic (with transliteration) saying what time your favorite movie usually starts, using a specific time.
items.answer: Example: يَبْدَأُ فِيلْمِي المُفَضَّلُ السَّاعَةَ الثَّامِنَةَ (yabda'u fīlmī l-mufaḍḍalu s-sāʿata th-thāminah) — 'My favorite movie starts at eight o'clock.'

items.prompt: Correct the error: نَحْنُ زُرْتُ الحَرَمَ الشَّرِيفَ فِي مَكَّةَ (naḥnu zurtu l-ḥarama sh-sharīfa fī makkah) — 'We visited the Sacred Mosque in Mecca.'
items.answer: نَحْنُ زُرْنَا الحَرَمَ الشَّرِيفَ فِي مَكَّةَ (naḥnu zurnā l-ḥarama sh-sharīfa fī makkah) — verb must agree with 'we' (نَحْنُ)

items.prompt: Complete with the correct word: أنا ___ في شركة كبيرة (ana ___ fī sharikatin kabīrah) — 'I work in a big company.' (use the correct form of 'to work')
items.answer: أعملُ (a'malu) — 'أنا أعملُ في شركة كبيرة' (ana a'malu fī sharikatin kabīrah)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb اتصل (ittaṣala — 'to call/contact') in the present tense for أنتِ (anti — 'you', feminine singular).
items.answer: تتصلينَ (tattaṣilīna) — 'أنتِ تتصلينَ' (anti tattaṣilīna) — 'you (f.) call'

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'Please call me on my cell phone.'
items.answer: من فضلك، اتصل بي على هاتفي المحمول (min faḍlik, ittaṣil bī 'alā hātifī al-maḥmūl)

items.prompt: Translate into English: هل لديك بريد إلكتروني؟ (hal ladayka barīd iliktrōnī?)
items.answer: 'Do you have an email (address)?'

items.prompt: Find and fix the mistake: المديرة ذهبَ إلى المكتب (al-mudīrah dhahaba ilā al-maktab) — 'The (female) manager went to the office.'
items.answer: المديرة ذهبَتْ إلى المكتب (al-mudīrah dhahabat ilā al-maktab) — the verb must agree in gender with the feminine subject 'المديرة'

items.prompt: What is the Arabic word for 'computer'? Give the word and its transliteration.
items.answer: حاسوب (ḥāsūb) — also commonly كمبيوتر (kombyūtar)

items.prompt: Complete: أرسلتُ لكَ ___ عبر البريد الإلكتروني (arsaltu laka ___ 'abra al-barīd al-iliktrōnī) — 'I sent you a message via email.'
items.answer: رسالة (risālah) — 'أرسلتُ لكَ رسالة عبر البريد الإلكتروني'

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb يعملُ (ya'malu — 'to work') in the present tense for نحن (naḥnu — 'we').
items.answer: نعملُ (na'malu) — 'نحن نعملُ' (naḥnu na'malu) — 'we work'

items.prompt: Translate to Arabic: "office" (as in workplace)
items.answer: مكتب (maktab)

items.prompt: Translate to Arabic: "telephone number"
items.answer: رقم الهاتف (raqam al-hātif)

items.prompt: Complete: أنا أعمل في ___ كبيرة (ʾanā aʿmalu fī ___ kabīrah) — "I work at a big company."
items.answer: شركة (sharikah)

items.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct preposition: أتصل ___ الهاتف بصديقي (ʾattaṣilu ___ al-hātif bi-ṣadīqī) — "I call my friend by phone."
items.answer: عن طريق / بواسطة الهاتف — but simplest: أتصل بصديقي عبر الهاتف — accepted answer: عبر (ʿabra) or بـ (bi-) — Standard idiom: أتصل بـ (attaṣilu bi-) + person, so correct fill is بصديقي already uses bi-; the blank should be omitted — Accept: بـ (bi-)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb أرسل (ʾarsala, "to send") in the present tense (المضارع) for هي (hiya, "she"): تُرسل رسالة إلكترونية (___ risālah ʾiliktrūniyyah) — "She sends an email."
items.answer: تُرسل (tursilu)

items.prompt: Conjugate طبع (ṭabaʿa, "to print") in the present tense for نحن (naḥnu, "we"): ___ الأوراق الآن (___ al-ʾawrāq al-ʾān) — "We are printing the papers now."
items.answer: نطبع (naṭbaʿu)

items.prompt: Find and correct the error: أنا يتكلم في الهاتف مع المدير (ʾanā yatakallamu fī al-hātif maʿa al-mudīr) — "I am talking on the phone with the manager."
items.answer: أنا أتكلم في الهاتف مع المدير (ʾanā ʾatakallamu fī al-hātif maʿa al-mudīr) — the verb must agree with أنا, so أتكلم not يتكلم

items.prompt: Translate to English: البريد الإلكتروني (al-barīd al-ʾiliktrūnī)
items.answer: email / electronic mail

items.prompt: In Arabic, what word means "computer"? Give the word and its transliteration.
items.answer: حاسوب (ḥāsūb) or كمبيوتر (kombyūtar)

items.prompt: Complete: هل يمكنني ترك ___؟ (hal yumkinunī tark ___?) — "May I leave a message?"
items.answer: رسالة (risālah)

items.prompt: Translate to Arabic: "The internet connection is slow today."
items.answer: الاتصال بالإنترنت بطيء اليوم (al-ittiṣāl bi-al-ʾintarnit baṭīʾ al-yawm)

items.prompt: Read: اجتماع العمل سيبدأ الساعة العاشرة صباحًا في قاعة المؤتمرات (ijtimāʿ al-ʿamal sa-yabdaʾu al-sāʿah al-ʿāshirah ṣabāḥan fī qāʿat al-muʾtamarāt). What time does the meeting start, and where?
items.answer: At 10:00 AM, in the conference room/hall

items.answer: Soccer/football

items.answer: أُحِبُّ أَنْ أَسْبَحَ فِي البَحْرِ (uḥibbu an asbaḥa fī al-baḥr)

items.prompt: Complete with the correct present-tense verb form: أَنَا ___ الْمُوسِيقَى كُلَّ يَوْمٍ (I listen to music every day) — أَنَا ___ الْمُوسِيقَى (anā ___ al-mūsīqā)
items.answer: أَسْتَمِعُ إِلَى (astamiʿu ilā)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb لَعِبَ (laʿiba, 'to play') in the present tense for هُوَ (huwa, 'he') and هِيَ (hiya, 'she').
items.answer: هُوَ يَلْعَبُ (huwa yalʿabu); هِيَ تَلْعَبُ (hiya talʿabu)

items.prompt: Find and correct the grammatical error: أَنَا يَذْهَبُ إِلَى الجَبَلِ فِي الصَّيْفِ (anā yadhhabu ilā al-jabal fī al-ṣayf) — 'I go to the mountain in summer.'
items.answer: Should be أَنَا أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الجَبَلِ فِي الصَّيْفِ (anā adhhabu ilā al-jabal fī al-ṣayf) — the verb must agree with 'I' (أَذْهَبُ), not the 'he' form (يَذْهَبُ).

items.prompt: Answer in Arabic (one short sentence) using transliteration: مَاذَا تُفَضِّلُ، الجَبَلُ أَمِ البَحْرُ؟ (mādhā tufaḍḍilu, al-jabal am al-baḥr? — 'What do you prefer, the mountain or the sea?')
items.answer: Any grammatically correct sentence such as: أُفَضِّلُ البَحْرَ (ufaḍḍilu al-baḥr) — 'I prefer the sea.'

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct Arabic word for 'guitar': هُوَ يَعْزِفُ عَلَى الـ___ (huwa yaʿzifu ʿalā al-___)
items.answer: جِيتَار (jītār)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic (with transliteration): 'We are going hiking in the forest this weekend.'
items.answer: سَنَقُومُ بِرِحْلَةٍ إِلَى الغَابَةِ فِي عُطْلَةِ نِهَايَةِ الأُسْبُوعِ (sanaqūmu bi-riḥlatin ilā al-ghābati fī ʿuṭlati nihāyati al-usbūʿ)

items.prompt: Translate into English: كُرَة القَدَم (kurat al-qadam)

items.answer: حَمَّام سِباحة (hammam sibaha)

items.prompt: Complete: أنا أُحِبُّ أن ______ (asma' al-musiqa) في المساء. (I like to listen to music in the evening.)
items.answer: أَسْمَعَ الموسيقى (asma' al-musiqa)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb يَلْعَب (yal'ab, 'to play') in the present tense for 'هي' (hiya, she).
items.answer: تَلْعَب (tal'ab)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb يَسْبَح (yasbah, 'to swim') in the present tense for 'نحن' (nahnu, we).
items.answer: نَسْبَح (nasbah)

items.prompt: Correct the error: أنا يلعب كرة السلة كل يوم. (I play basketball every day.)
items.answer: أنا أَلْعَب كرة السلة كل يوم. (ana al'ab kurat as-salla kulla yawm) — verb must agree with 'أنا' (ana) subject, using أَلْعَب not يلعب.

items.answer: جَبَل (jabal)

items.prompt: Translate into English: الغِناء (al-ghina')
items.answer: singing

items.prompt: Answer in Arabic with a full sentence: ماذا تُحِبُّ أن تفعل في عُطلة نهاية الأسبوع؟ (What do you like to do on the weekend?) — Use at least one recreation vocabulary word.
items.answer: Answers vary; example: أنا أُحِبُّ أن أَمْشِيَ في الجَبَل. (ana uhibbu an amshiya fi al-jabal) — 'I like to hike in the mountain.'

items.prompt: Complete with the correct present-tense verb form: هم ______ (يعزف - ya'zif, 'to play an instrument') الجيتار كل مساء. (They play guitar every evening.)
items.answer: يَعْزِفون (ya'zifun)

items.prompt: Translate into English: نَتَنَزَّه في الغابة (natanazzah fi al-ghaba)
items.answer: We take a walk/stroll in the forest

items.prompt: Correct the error in this sentence: أنا أَسْمَع الموسيقى بِعَيْني. (I listen to music with my eyes.)
items.answer: أنا أَسْمَع الموسيقى بِأُذُني. (ana asma' al-musiqa bi-udhuni) — should be 'ear' (أُذُن, udhun) not 'eye' (عَيْن, 'ayn) since listening uses ears.

items.prompt: Complete with the correct word: أريد أن أُبَدِّلَ مئة دولار إلى ______ (I want to exchange one hundred dollars into ______, meaning 'dinars').
items.answer: دنانير (danānīr)

items.prompt: Translate into English: سعر الصرف (si‘r aṣ-ṣarf)
items.answer: exchange rate

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb بَدَّلَ (baddala, 'to exchange/change') in the past tense for أنا (anā, 'I') and نحن (naḥnu, 'we').
items.answer: أنا بَدَّلْتُ (anā baddaltu) — I exchanged; نحن بَدَّلْنَا (naḥnu baddalnā) — we exchanged

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'Where is the nearest bank?'
items.answer: أين أقرب بنك؟ (ayna aqrabu bank?)

items.prompt: Translate into English: أين يمكنني أن أصرف شيكاً سياحياً؟ (ayna yumkinunī an aṣrifa shīkan siyāḥiyyan?)
items.answer: Where can I cash a traveler's check?

items.prompt: Find and fix the grammatical error: البنك مفتوحة كل يوم ما عدا الجمعة (al-bank maftūḥah kull yawm mā ‘adā al-jum‘ah) — 'The bank is open every day except Friday.'
items.answer: البنك مفتوحٌ كل يوم ما عدا الجمعة (al-bank maftūḥ...) — بنك is masculine, so the adjective must be مفتوح, not مفتوحة.

items.prompt: In Arabic, write one full sentence asking a bank clerk what documents (وثائق, wathā’iq) you need to open an account (حساب, ḥisāb).
items.answer: Sample answer: ما هي الوثائق التي أحتاجها لفتح حساب؟ (mā hiya al-wathā’iq allatī aḥtājuhā li-fatḥ ḥisāb?)

items.prompt: Complete with the correct word: هل يمكنني أن أستخدم ______ لسحب النقود من الآلة؟ (Can I use my ______ to withdraw cash from the machine? — meaning 'card')
items.answer: بطاقتي (biṭāqatī)

items.prompt: أريد أن أُغَيِّرَ الدولارات إلى ...... (I want to exchange dollars into ______ - fill in the Arabic word for 'currency').
items.answer: عُملة (‘umla) - 'currency'. Full sentence: أريد أن أغيّر الدولارات إلى عملة أخرى (I want to exchange the dollars for another currency).

items.prompt: Translate into English: أين أقرب صرّاف آلي؟ (Ayna aqrab ṣarrāf ālī?)
items.answer: Where is the nearest ATM?

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'I would like to open a bank account.'
items.answer: أريد أن أفتح حسابًا في البنك (Urīdu an aftaḥa ḥisāban fī al-bank).

items.prompt: Complete with the correct preposition: صرفتُ نقودي ...... دولارات (Ṣaraftu nuqūdī ______ dūlārāt) - 'I exchanged my money into dollars.'
items.answer: إلى (ilā) - 'into/to'. Full sentence: صرفتُ نقودي إلى دولارات.

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb صَرَفَ (ṣarafa, 'to exchange/spend') in the present tense (المضارع) for: هو (huwa), هي (hiya), نحن (naḥnu).
items.answer: هو يَصرِف (huwa yaṣrifu) - he exchanges; هي تَصرِف (hiya taṣrifu) - she exchanges; نحن نَصرِف (naḥnu naṣrifu) - we exchange.

items.prompt: Find and fix the error: أنا يصرف نقود في البنك (Anā yaṣrifu nuqūd fī al-bank) - intended meaning: 'I exchange money at the bank.'
items.answer: The verb should agree with the first-person subject: أنا أَصرِف نقودًا في البنك (Anā aṣrifu nuqūdan fī al-bank).

items.prompt: You see a sign at a currency exchange counter: سعر الصرف اليوم: دولار واحد يساوي عشرة جنيهات (Si‘r al-ṣarf al-yawm: dūlār wāḥid yusāwī ‘asharat junayhāt). Question: how many local pounds does one dollar equal, according to this sign?
items.answer: Ten pounds (عشرة جنيهات, ‘asharat junayhāt).

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the Arabic word for 'credit card': هل تقبلون الدفع بـ ...... ؟ (Hal taqbalūna al-daf‘a bi- ______ ? - 'Do you accept payment by credit card?')
items.answer: بطاقة الائتمان (biṭāqat al-i’timān) - 'credit card'.

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'Can I pay in cash?'
items.answer: هل يمكنني الدفع نقدًا؟ (Hal yumkinunī al-daf‘u naqdan?)

items.prompt: Write one full Arabic sentence (with transliteration) asking a bank teller what the exchange rate is today.
items.answer: Example: ما هو سعر الصرف اليوم؟ (Mā huwa si‘r al-ṣarf al-yawm? - 'What is the exchange rate today?')

items.prompt: Correct the gender agreement error: البنك مفتوحة يوم السبت (Al-bank maftūḥa yawm al-sabt) - intended: 'The bank is open on Saturday.'
items.answer: البنك is masculine, so it should be: البنك مفتوح يوم السبت (Al-bank maftūḥ yawm al-sabt).

items.prompt: Complete: وقّعتُ الـ ...... قبل أن أستلم النقود (Waqqa‘tu al- ______ qabla an astalima al-nuqūd) - 'I signed the ______ before I received the money.' (fill with 'check' in Arabic)
items.answer: شيك (shīk) - 'check'. Full sentence: وقّعتُ الشيك قبل أن أستلم النقود.

items.prompt: Complete with the correct form of يُخَطِّط (yukhaTTiT, 'to plan'): نَحنُ ___ لِرِحلةٍ إلى مِصر الأسبوعَ القادِم (naHnu ___ li-riHlatin ila miSr al-usbū'a al-qādim) — 'We are planning a trip to Egypt next week.'
items.answer: نُخَطِّط (nukhaTTiT) — نَحنُ نُخَطِّط لِرِحلةٍ إلى مِصر الأسبوعَ القادِم

items.prompt: Conjugate يَحجُز (yaHjiz, 'to book/reserve') in the present tense for هِي (hiya, 'she'). Write the full sentence: هِي ___ فُندُقًا في القاهِرة (hiya ___ funduqan fī al-qāhira) — 'She books/is booking a hotel in Cairo.'
items.answer: تَحجُز (taHjiz) — هِي تَحجُز فُندُقًا في القاهِرة

items.prompt: Translate into English: هَل حَجَزتَ الفُندُق وتَذكِرة الطائِرة؟ (hal Hajazta al-funduq wa-tadhkirat aT-Tā'ira?)
items.answer: Did you book the hotel and the plane ticket?

items.answer: أحتاجُ إلى جَوازِ سَفَرٍ وتَذكِرةٍ قَبلَ الرِحلة (aHtāju ilā jawāzi safarin wa-tadhkiratin qabla ar-riHla)

items.prompt: Find and fix the grammatical error: أنا سَوفَ يُسافِر غَدًا إلى بَيروت (anā sawfa yusāfir ghadan ilā beirūt) — meant to say 'I will travel tomorrow to Beirut.'
items.answer: أنا سَوفَ أُسافِرُ غَدًا إلى بَيروت (anā sawfa usāfiru ghadan ilā beirūt) — the verb must match the first-person subject 'أنا' (anā), so يُسافِر becomes أُسافِر.

items.prompt: In Arabic, name three items you should pack in your حَقيبة السَفَر (Haqibat as-safar, 'suitcase') before a trip.
items.answer: Any three reasonable travel items, e.g.: جَوازُ سَفَر (jawāzu safar, passport)، مَلابِس (malābis, clothes)، تَذكِرة (tadhkira, ticket)، فُرشاةُ أسنان (furshātu asnān, toothbrush)

items.prompt: Complete with the correct verb: يَجِبُ أن ___ جَوازَ السَفَرِ قَبلَ الرِحلة (yajibu an ___ jawāza as-safari qabla ar-riHla) — 'You must renew your passport before the trip.' (verb: يُجَدِّد, yujaddid, 'to renew')
items.answer: تُجَدِّدَ (tujaddida) — يَجِبُ أن تُجَدِّدَ جَوازَ السَفَرِ قَبلَ الرِحلة

items.prompt: Conjugate يُخَطِّط (yukhaTTiT, 'to plan') in the present tense for هُم (hum, 'they'). Write the full sentence: هُم ___ لِرِحلةٍ طَويلة (hum ___ li-riHlatin Tawīla) — 'They are planning a long trip.'
items.answer: يُخَطِّطون (yukhaTTiTūn) — هُم يُخَطِّطون لِرِحلةٍ طَويلة

items.prompt: Translate to English: الحقيبة (al-ḥaqībah)
items.answer: the suitcase/bag

items.prompt: Translate to Arabic (with transliteration): 'passport'
items.answer: جواز السفر (jawāz as-safar)

items.prompt: Complete with the correct preposition: سَأُسافِرُ ___ مِصْرَ الأُسْبوعَ القادِمَ (sa-usāfiru ___ Miṣra al-usbūʿa al-qādima) 'I will travel to Egypt next week.'
items.answer: إلى (ilā)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb حَجَزَ (ḥajaza, 'to book/reserve') in the present tense (يَحْجِزُ / yaḥjizu) for 'we': نَحْنُ ___ (naḥnu ___) الفُنْدُقَ (al-funduqa)
items.answer: نَحْجِزُ (naḥjizu)

items.prompt: Translate to English: أَحْتاجُ إلى تَذْكِرَةِ طائِرَةٍ (aḥtāju ilā tadhkirati ṭāʾirah)
items.answer: I need an airplane ticket.

items.prompt: Find and correct the error: أَنا سَوْفَ يَذْهَبُ إلى المَطار (anā sawfa yadhhabu ilā al-maṭār) 'I will go to the airport.'
items.answer: أَنا سَوْفَ أَذْهَبُ إلى المَطار (anā sawfa adhhabu ilā al-maṭār) — the verb must agree with 'I' (أَذْهَبُ / adhhabu), not the 'he' form (يَذْهَبُ)

items.prompt: Complete: قَبْلَ السَّفَرِ، يَجِبُ أَنْ أُحَضِّرَ ___ (qabla as-safar, yajibu an uḥaḍḍira ___) 'Before the trip, I must prepare ___' (use the word for 'the luggage/bags')
items.answer: الحَقائِب (al-ḥaqāʾib)

items.prompt: In Arabic, write one full sentence saying you need to reserve a hotel room. Use حَجَزَ (ḥajaza) or a form of it.
items.answer: Sample: أَحْتاجُ أَنْ أَحْجِزَ غُرْفَةً فِي الفُنْدُقِ (aḥtāju an aḥjiza ghurfatan fī al-funduqi) 'I need to reserve a room in the hotel.'

items.prompt: Translate to Arabic (with transliteration): 'When does the plane leave?'
items.answer: مَتى تُقْلِعُ الطائِرَةُ؟ (matā tuqliʿu aṭ-ṭāʾirah?)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb سافَرَ (sāfara, 'to travel') in the past tense for 'they' (masculine plural): هُمْ ___ (hum ___) إلى لُبْنانَ (ilā Lubnān)
items.answer: سافَروا (sāfarū)

items.prompt: Complete with the correct question word: ___ سَتُسافِرُ؟ (___ satusāfiru?) 'When will you (m.) travel?'
items.answer: مَتى (matā)

items.prompt: Read and answer in English: تَحْتاجُ سارَة إلى تَأشيرَةٍ لِلسَّفَرِ إلى الهِنْد، لِذا ذَهَبَتْ إلى السِّفارَةِ (taḥtāju Sārah ilā taʾshiratin lis-safar ilā al-Hind, lidhā dhahabat ilā as-sifārah). Why did Sarah go to the embassy?
items.answer: Because she needs a visa to travel to India.

items.prompt: Translate into English: المطار (al-maṭār)
items.answer: the airport

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic (with transliteration): 'train station'
items.answer: محطة القطار (maḥaṭṭat al-qiṭār)

items.prompt: Complete with the correct preposition: أنا أسافر ___ الطائرة إلى القاهرة (anā usāfir ___ aṭ-ṭā'ira ilā al-Qāhira) — 'I travel by plane to Cairo.'
items.answer: بـ (bi-) → أسافر بالطائرة (usāfir bi-ṭ-ṭā'ira)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb سافر (sāfara, 'to travel') in the present tense (يفعل form) for هي (hiya, 'she').
items.answer: تُسَافِر (tusāfir) — 'she travels'

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb وصل (waṣala, 'to arrive') in the past tense for نحن (naḥnu, 'we').
items.answer: وَصَلْنَا (waṣalnā) — 'we arrived'

items.prompt: Find and correct the mistake: القطار يصل إلى محطة في الساعة خمسة (al-qiṭār yaṣil ilā maḥaṭṭa fī as-sā‘a khamsa) — meant to say 'The train arrives at the station at five o'clock.'
items.answer: Missing definite article: should be إلى المحطة (ilā al-maḥaṭṭa) — 'to the station', since 'station' here refers to a specific, known station.

items.prompt: Answer in Arabic (one short sentence) with transliteration: أين تشتري تذكرة القطار؟ (Ayna tashtarī tadhkarat al-qiṭār? — 'Where do you buy a train ticket?')
items.answer: أشتري تذكرة القطار في المحطة (Ashtarī tadhkarat al-qiṭār fī al-maḥaṭṭa) — 'I buy the train ticket at the station.'

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic (with transliteration): 'The taxi will take us to the airport tomorrow.'
items.answer: التاكسي سيأخذنا إلى المطار غدًا (at-tāksī sa-ya'khudhunā ilā al-maṭār ghadan)
