items.answer: محطة القطار (maHaTTat al-qiTaar)

items.prompt: Complete: أنا أسافر بـ ____ (ana usaafir bi-____) meaning 'I travel by plane.' Fill in the blank with the correct word for 'plane'.
items.answer: الطائرة (aT-Taa'ira)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb سافر (saafara, 'to travel') in the past tense for 'he' (huwa) and 'they' (masc. plural, hum).
items.answer: هو سافرَ (huwa saafara) — 'he traveled'; هم سافروا (hum saafaruu) — 'they traveled'

items.prompt: Correct the error in this sentence: أنا يذهب إلى المحطة بالسيارة (ana yadh-hab ilaa al-maHaTTa bis-sayyaara) — intended meaning: 'I go to the station by car.'
items.answer: أنا أذهب إلى المحطة بالسيارة (ana adh-hab ilaa al-maHaTTa bis-sayyaara) — the verb must match the subject 'I' (أذهب/adh-hab), not 'he' (يذهب/yadh-hab)

items.prompt: Complete the sentence: أريد تذكرة ____ إلى القاهرة (ureedu tadhkara ____ ilaa al-qaahira) meaning 'I want a one-way ticket to Cairo.' Fill in the missing word for 'one-way'.
items.answer: ذهاب فقط (dhahaab faqaT)

items.prompt: Translate into English: رصيف القطار (raSeef al-qiTaar)
items.answer: Train platform

items.prompt: In Arabic, what word means 'boarding pass' (used at the airport before flying)? Give the Arabic word with transliteration.
items.answer: بطاقة الصعود (biTaaqat aS-Su'uud)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb وصل (waSala, 'to arrive') in the present tense for 'I' (ana) and 'we' (naHnu).
items.answer: أنا أصِل (ana aSil) — 'I arrive'; نحن نصِل (naHnu naSil) — 'we arrive'

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic (with transliteration): 'The bus is late.'
items.answer: الحافلة متأخرة (al-Haafila muta'akh-khira)

items.prompt: Correct the error in this sentence: هم سافرت بالقطار أمس (hum saafarat bil-qiTaar amsi) — intended meaning: 'They traveled by train yesterday.'
items.answer: هم سافروا بالقطار أمس (hum saafaruu bil-qiTaar amsi) — the verb must agree with the plural subject 'هم' (hum), using سافروا (saafaruu), not the feminine singular سافرت (saafarat)

items.prompt: What is the Arabic word for 'passport,' commonly needed when boarding a plane? Give the word with transliteration.
items.answer: جواز السفر (jawaaz as-safar)

items.prompt: Complete the question with the correct Arabic word for 'vacant/free': هل عندكم غرفة ___؟ (Hal ‘indakum ghurfa ____؟) — 'Do you have a vacant room?'
items.answer: شاغرة (shāghira) — e.g. هل عندكم غرفة شاغرة؟ (Hal ‘indakum ghurfa shāghira?)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb حجز (ḥajaza, 'to reserve/book') in the present tense for أنا (I) and هي (she).
items.answer: أنا أحجز (anā aḥjuzu) — I reserve; هي تحجز (hiya taḥjuzu) — she reserves

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'I want to book a room for three nights.'
items.answer: أريد أن أحجز غرفة لثلاث ليالٍ (Urīdu an aḥjuza ghurfatan lithalāthi layālin)

items.prompt: Translate into English: كم تكلفة الليلة الواحدة؟ (Kam taklifat al-layla al-wāḥida?)
items.answer: How much does one night cost?

items.prompt: Find and correct the agreement mistake: أنا حجزت غرفتين كبير (Anā ḥajazt ghurfatayn kabīr) — 'I booked two big rooms.'
items.answer: أنا حجزت غرفتين كبيرتين (Anā ḥajazt ghurfatayn kabīratayn) — the adjective must agree in dual/feminine form.

items.prompt: What is the Arabic word for the hotel 'reception/front desk'?
items.answer: الاستقبال (al-istiqbāl)

items.prompt: Complete the question with the word for 'breakfast': هل السعر يشمل ___؟ (Hal as-si‘r yashmalu ____؟) — 'Does the price include breakfast?'
items.answer: الفطور (al-futūr) — هل السعر يشمل الفطور؟ (Hal as-si‘r yashmalu al-futūr?)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'Is there Wi-Fi in the room?'
items.answer: هل يوجد واي فاي في الغرفة؟ (Hal yūjad wāy fāy fī al-ghurfa?)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'hotel'
items.answer: فُنْدُق (funduq)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'reservation'
items.answer: حَجْز (ḥajz)

items.prompt: Complete: أُرِيدُ ____ غُرْفَةً لِلَيْلَتَيْنِ (urīdu ____ ghurfatan lilaylatayn) — 'I want to book a room for two nights.'
items.answer: أَحْجِزَ (aḥjiza)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb حَجَزَ (ḥajaza, 'to book/reserve') in the present tense (المضارع) for أنا (anā, I), أنتَ (anta, you m.), and هي (hiya, she).
items.answer: أنا أَحْجِزُ (anā aḥjizu), أنتَ تَحْجِزُ (anta taḥjizu), هي تَحْجِزُ (hiya taḥjizu)

items.prompt: Translate into English: هَلْ يُوجَدُ حَمَّامٌ خَاصٌّ فِي الغُرْفَةِ؟ (hal yūjadu ḥammāmun khāṣṣun fī al-ghurfa?)
items.answer: Is there a private bathroom in the room?

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'How much does the room cost per night?'
items.answer: كَمْ تُكَلِّفُ الغُرْفَةُ فِي اللَّيْلَةِ؟ (kam tukallifu al-ghurfatu fī al-layla?)

items.prompt: Complete: الغُرْفَةُ فِيهَا سَرِيرَانِ، فَهِيَ غُرْفَةٌ ____ (al-ghurfatu fīhā sarīrān, fahiya ghurfatun ____) — 'The room has two beds, so it's a double room.'
items.answer: مُزْدَوِجَة (muzdawija)

items.prompt: Correct the error in this sentence: أَنَا أُرِيدُ حَجَزَ غُرْفَةً (anā urīdu ḥajaza ghurfatan) — intended meaning: 'I want to reserve a room.'
items.answer: أَنَا أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَحْجِزَ غُرْفَةً (anā urīdu an aḥjiza ghurfatan) — need أَنْ + subjunctive verb after urīdu, not the past tense form.

items.prompt: In Arabic, write one full sentence asking the receptionist (المُوَظَّف, al-muwaẓẓaf) whether breakfast is included in the price.
items.answer: Sample correct answer: هَلْ الإِفْطَارُ مَشْمُولٌ فِي السِّعْرِ؟ (hal al-ifṭāru mashmūlun fī as-siʿr?)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'key' and 'floor (story of a building)'
items.answer: مِفْتَاح (miftāḥ) and طَابِق (ṭābiq)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb وَصَلَ (waṣala, 'to arrive') in the past tense (الماضي) for نَحْنُ (naḥnu, we) and هُم (hum, they).
items.answer: نَحْنُ وَصَلْنَا (naḥnu waṣalnā), هُم وَصَلُوا (hum waṣalū)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic: 'We would like to check out tomorrow morning.'
items.answer: نُرِيدُ أَنْ نُغَادِرَ الفُنْدُقَ صَبَاحَ غَدٍ (nurīdu an nughādira al-funduqa ṣabāḥa ghadin)

items.prompt: Translate into English: النَّجدة! اتَّصِل بِالإسْعاف! (an-najda! ittasil bil-is‘āf!)
items.answer: Help! Call an ambulance!

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word for 'police': اتَّصِلي بِـ ___ حالًا! (ittasilī bi-___ ḥālan!) — meaning 'Call the police immediately!' (feminine command)
items.answer: الشُّرْطة (ash-shurṭa)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb سَرَقَ (saraqa, 'to steal') in the past tense for 'he' and 'they (masc. pl.)': رَجُلٌ ___ حَقيبَتي وَهَرَبَ (rajulun ___ ḥaqībatī wa haraba) = 'A man ___ my bag and fled.' Then give the form for 'they stole'.
items.answer: he: سَرَقَ (saraqa); they: سَرَقوا (saraqū)

items.prompt: Find and fix the grammatical error in this sentence: أنا مُحتاجٌ إلى طَبيب حالًا لِأنَّني مَريضة (anā muḥtājun ilā ṭabīb ḥālan li’annanī marīḍa) — intended meaning: 'I (fem.) need a doctor right now because I am sick.'
items.answer: مُحتاجٌ (masc.) should be مُحتاجةٌ (muḥtājatun) to agree with the feminine speaker (marīḍa).

items.prompt: Read this sentence and answer in English: تَعَرَّضَتِ السَّيّارةُ لِحادِثٍ خَطيرٍ، وَنُقِلَ السّائِقُ إلى المُستَشفى بِسَيّارةِ الإسْعاف (ta‘arraḍatis-sayyāratu li-ḥādithin khaṭīrin, wa nuqila as-sā’iqu ilā al-mustashfā bi-sayyāratil-is‘āf). Question: What happened to the driver?
items.answer: He was seriously injured in a car accident and was taken to the hospital by ambulance.

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic (with transliteration in your answer): 'There is a fire! Get out of the building!'
items.answer: هُناكَ حَريقٌ! اُخرُجْ مِنَ المَبْنى! (hunāka ḥarīqun! ukhruj mina al-mabnā!)

items.prompt: Complete with the correct preposition: أنا في حاجةٍ ___ مُحامٍ لِأنَّني اُتُّهِمْتُ ظُلمًا (anā fī ḥājatin ___ muḥāmin li’annanī uttuhimtu ẕulman) = 'I need a lawyer because I was falsely accused.'
items.answer: إلى (ilā)

items.prompt: In Arabic, write one short sentence (3-5 words) telling someone to call the fire department, using an imperative verb. Include transliteration.
items.answer: Example: اتَّصِلْ بِالمَطافِئ! (ittasil bil-maṭāfi’!) = 'Call the fire department!'

items.prompt: Translate to English: النجدة! (an-najda!)
items.answer: Help! (a distress call, like 'Help!' or 'Mayday!')

items.prompt: Translate to Arabic script (with transliteration): 'Call an ambulance!'
items.answer: اتصل بسيارة الإسعاف! (ittasil bi-sayyārat al-isʿāf!)

items.prompt: Fill in the blank: أنا بحاجة إلى ___ لأن يدي تنزف. (anā bi-ḥāja ilā ___ li-anna yadī tanzif.) — 'I need a ___ because my hand is bleeding.' (word for 'bandage')
items.answer: ضمادة (ḍimāda)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb اتصل (ittaṣala, 'to call/contact') in the past tense for أنتِ (anti, 'you' fem. sing.).
items.answer: اتصلتِ (ittaṣalti)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb سرق (saraqa, 'to steal') in the present tense for هم (hum, 'they' masc. plural).
items.answer: يسرقون (yasriqūn)

items.prompt: Correct the grammatical error: أنا رأيت حادثة أمس في الشارع. (anā ra'aytu ḥādithatan ams fī ash-shāriʿ.) — the speaker is male, but the verb form used is meant for a different subject. Find and fix the mismatch between the pronoun أنا and the verb form (it should show 1st person singular past correctly formatted; the sentence as given already looks correct except that ams needs no tanwīn on حادثة). Fix the incorrect tanwīn.
items.answer: أنا رأيت حادثةً أمس في الشارع should be أنا رأيت حادثة أمس في الشارع (ḥādithatan is incorrect here since the noun is definite in context of a specific past event; remove the extra fatḥatayn) — corrected: أنا رأيت الحادثة أمس في الشارع (anā ra'aytu al-ḥāditha ams fī ash-shāriʿ) 'I saw the accident yesterday in the street.'

items.prompt: In Arabic, write one short sentence (3-5 words) telling someone to call the police. Use the word شرطة (shurṭa, 'police').
items.answer: Example: اتصل بالشرطة! (ittaṣil bish-shurṭa!) 'Call the police!'

items.prompt: Translate to English: أنا بحاجة إلى محامٍ. (anā bi-ḥāja ilā muḥāmin.)
items.answer: I need a lawyer.

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct form of the imperative verb 'run' (هرب/يهرب - to flee/run away) addressing a group of men: ___ من هنا الآن! (___ min hunā al-ān!) — 'Run from here now!'
items.answer: اهربوا (ihrubū)

items.prompt: Write a full sentence in Arabic (with transliteration) explaining that there is a fire in the building. Use the word حريق (ḥarīq, 'fire').
items.answer: Example: هناك حريق في المبنى! (hunāka ḥarīq fī al-mabnā!) 'There is a fire in the building!'

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb كسر (kasara, 'to break') in the past tense for هي (hiya, 'she') — as in 'she broke her leg.'
items.answer: كسرت (kasarat)

items.prompt: Translate to Arabic script (with transliteration): 'Where is the nearest hospital?'
items.answer: أين أقرب مستشفى؟ (ayna aqrab mustashfā?)

items.prompt: Translate into English: مَرْحَبًا، كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟ (marHaban, kayfa Haaluka?)
items.answer: Hello, how are you? (spoken to a male)

items.prompt: Fill the blank with the correct word for 'thank you': ...، هَذَا لَذِيذٌ جِدًّا (___, haadhaa ladheedhun jiddan) meaning 'Thank you, this is very delicious.'
items.answer: شُكْرًا (shukran)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb تَعَلَّمَ (ta'allama, 'to learn') in the present tense (المضارع) for أَنَا (ana, 'I').
items.answer: أَتَعَلَّمُ (ata'allamu) - 'I learn/am learning'

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb سَافَرَ (saafara, 'to travel') in the past tense (الماضي) for هُمْ (hum, 'they, masc. plural').
items.answer: سَافَرُوا (saafaruu) - 'they traveled'

items.prompt: Find and fix the mistake in this sentence meant to say 'I practice Arabic every day': أَنَا يُمَارِسُ العَرَبِيَّةَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ (ana yumaarisu al-'arabiyyata kulla yawmin)
items.answer: أَنَا أُمَارِسُ العَرَبِيَّةَ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ (ana umaarisu al-'arabiyyata kulla yawmin) - the verb must agree with 'I' (أُمَارِسُ), not the 'he' form (يُمَارِسُ)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic (with transliteration): 'I listen to Arabic songs to improve my listening.'
items.answer: أَسْتَمِعُ إِلَى الأَغَانِي العَرَبِيَّةِ لِأُحَسِّنَ اسْتِمَاعِي (astami'u ilaa al-aghaani al-'arabiyyati li-uHassina istimaa'ii)

items.prompt: In your own words (English is fine), name one practical daily habit mentioned in this unit's theme that could help a learner absorb Arabic faster, and explain briefly why it works.
items.answer: Answers vary; a valid example: watching Arabic TV shows/movies with subtitles helps train the ear to recognize sounds and rhythm of spoken Arabic in context.

items.prompt: Complete with the correct possessive suffix meaning 'my friend' (male friend): صَدِيق___ (Sadiiq___)
items.answer: صَدِيقِي (Sadiiqii) - 'my friend'

items.prompt: Translate to English: مرحبا، كيف حالك؟ (marHaban, kayfa Haaluka?)
items.answer: Hello, how are you? (to a male)

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct possessive suffix meaning 'my': هذا كتاب_____ (haadhaa kitaab___) = 'This is my book'
items.answer: ي (-ii) → كتابي (kitaabii)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb تَعَلَّمَ (ta'allama, 'he learned') in the present tense for أنا (anaa, 'I'): أنا _____ اللغة العربية (anaa ___ al-lughah al-'arabiyyah)
items.answer: أتعلّم (ata'allamu) — 'I am learning/I learn'

items.prompt: Name one everyday strategy mentioned for picking up Arabic quickly that involves listening to native speakers regularly (in English, one sentence).
items.answer: Answers vary; acceptable example: Watch or listen to Arabic media (news, songs, shows) daily to train your ear.

items.prompt: Correct the grammatical error: أنا يذهب إلى السوق (anaa yadh-habu ilaa as-suuq) — intended meaning: 'I go to the market.'
items.answer: أنا أذهب إلى السوق (anaa adhhabu ilaa as-suuq) — the verb must agree with 'I', not 'he'.

items.prompt: Translate to Arabic: 'I practice Arabic every day.'
items.answer: أتدرّب على العربية كل يوم (atadarrabu 'alaa al-'arabiyyah kulla yawm)

items.prompt: Fill in the missing word: من المفيد أن تكتب _____ جديدة كل يوم (min al-mufiid an taktuba ___ jadiidah kulla yawm) = 'It's useful to write new vocabulary every day.'
items.answer: كلمات (kalimaat) — 'words/vocabulary'

items.prompt: In one sentence (English), explain why finding a language partner is considered a helpful strategy for learning Arabic quickly.
items.answer: Answers vary; acceptable example: A language partner gives you real conversation practice and immediate feedback.

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb سَمِعَ (sami'a, 'he heard/listened') in the present tense for نحن (naHnu, 'we'): نحن _____ إلى الأخبار العربية (naHnu ___ ilaa al-akhbaar al-'arabiyyah)
items.answer: نسمع (nasma'u) — 'we listen'

items.prompt: Translate to English: من الأفضل أن تسافر إلى بلد عربي لتتعلّم اللغة بسرعة (min al-afDal an tusaafira ilaa balad 'arabiyy litata'allama al-lughah bisur'ah).
items.answer: It's better to travel to an Arabic-speaking country to learn the language quickly.

items.prompt: Correct the error in word choice: أحب أن أقرأ الجرائد لأتحسّن نطقي (uHibbu an aqra'a al-jaraa'id li-ataHassana nuTqii) — intended meaning: 'I like to read newspapers to improve my listening.'
items.answer: The sentence describes 'pronunciation' (نطق, nuTq), not listening. Should use استماعي (istimaa'ii) — 'my listening': لأتحسّن استماعي (li-ataHassana istimaa'ii)

items.prompt: Write one full Arabic sentence (with transliteration) describing a daily habit you could use to pick up Arabic quickly, e.g. listening, writing, or speaking practice.
items.answer: Answers vary; acceptable example: أستمع إلى الأغاني العربية كل صباح (astami'u ilaa al-aghaanii al-'arabiyyah kulla SabaaH) — 'I listen to Arabic songs every morning.'

items.prompt: Translate into English: إن شاء الله (in shā' allāh)
items.answer: God willing / hopefully

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic script with transliteration: 'Thank God' (used when things are fine or after finishing something)
items.answer: الحمد لله (al-ḥamdu lillāh)

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct expression: When someone sneezes, you say ___ (al-ḥamdu lillāh / yislamū / al-ḥamdu lillāh) — actually to the sneezer you say 'yarḥamuka Allāh' (يرحمك الله). Fill in: You would respond to 'يرحمك الله' (yarḥamuka allāh) by saying ___.
items.answer: يهديكم الله (yahdīkum allāh) - 'may God guide you', a common response

items.prompt: In your own words (English), explain when an Arabic speaker would say مع السلامة (ma'a as-salāma) rather than إلى اللقاء (ilā al-liqā').
items.answer: مع السلامة (ma'a as-salāma) means 'go with safety/peace' and is used specifically when someone is leaving or departing, wishing them a safe journey/farewell; إلى اللقاء (ilā al-liqā') is a more neutral 'see you later/until we meet again' used in any parting.

items.prompt: Correct the error in this sentence. The learner wrote: إن شاء الله (in shā' allāh) meaning 'thank God' after finishing a task. What is wrong, and what expression should be used instead?
items.answer: إن شاء الله (in shā' allāh) means 'God willing' and refers to future hope/intention, not thanks. After finishing a task, the correct expression is الحمد لله (al-ḥamdu lillāh), 'thank God/praise be to God'.

items.prompt: Fill in the blank: When you want to compliment someone's new possession or achievement, Arabic speakers often say ما شاء الله (___ shā' allāh) to ward off the evil eye/jealousy.
items.answer: ما (mā)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic script with transliteration: 'No problem / you're welcome' (a common polite response after being thanked or after helping someone)
items.answer: عفواً (‘afwan) or لا شكر على واجب (lā shukr ‘alā wājib)

items.prompt: Read this short exchange and answer in English: أحمد: شكراً جزيلاً! (Aḥmad: shukran jazīlan!) — سارة: عفواً، لا شكر على واجب. (Sāra: ‘afwan, lā shukr ‘alā wājib.) What is Ahmad doing, and what is the sense of Sara's reply?
items.answer: Ahmad is thanking Sara profusely ('thank you very much'), and Sara is politely dismissing the need for thanks, saying essentially 'you're welcome, no thanks needed for a duty/obligation' — i.e., it was nothing.

items.prompt: Translate this expression into English and describe a situation when you'd use it: إن شاء الله (in shā' Allāh)
items.answer: 'God willing' — used when talking about future plans or hopes, expressing that the outcome depends on God's will (e.g., 'I'll see you tomorrow, in shā' Allāh').

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic script with transliteration: 'Thank God' (used after saying you are well or after finishing something safely)
items.answer: الحمد لله (al-ḥamdu lillāh)

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct expression: When someone says الحمد لله (al-ḥamdu lillāh) after sneezing, the appropriate response is ______ (يرحمكم الله / ...).
items.answer: يرحمك الله (yarḥamuka Allāh) — 'God have mercy on you'

items.prompt: In your own words (English), explain the difference in usage between إن شاء الله (in shā' Allāh) and الحمد لله (al-ḥamdu lillāh). Give one example sentence context for each.
items.answer: إن شاء الله is used for future hopes/plans ('God willing, I will pass the exam'); الحمد لله is used to express gratitude or acknowledge a good outcome ('I finished the exam, thank God').

items.prompt: Translate into English: ما شاء الله (mā shā' Allāh)
items.answer: 'What God has willed' — an expression of admiration or to ward off the evil eye when complimenting someone or something.

items.prompt: A learner wrote: 'To say welcome to a guest, you should say مع السلامة (ma‘a as-salāma).' Correct the mistake and give the right expression for welcoming a guest.
items.answer: مع السلامة (ma‘a as-salāma) means 'goodbye/go safely,' used when someone is leaving. To welcome a guest, you say أهلاً وسهلاً (ahlan wa sahlan) — 'welcome.'

items.prompt: Complete the exchange: Person A: كيف الحال؟ (kayf al-ḥāl?) Person B: ______ (bism, meaning 'fine, thank God')
items.answer: الحمد لله، بخير (al-ḥamdu lillāh, bikhayr) — 'Thank God, I'm fine.'

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic script with transliteration: 'Welcome!' (said to someone arriving at your home)
items.answer: أهلاً وسهلاً (ahlan wa sahlan)

items.prompt: When would you say إن شاء الله (in shā' Allāh) instead of directly promising something, and why might this be culturally important in Arabic-speaking contexts?
items.answer: It's used when discussing future actions/plans to acknowledge that outcomes ultimately depend on God's will, reflecting humility and religious/cultural custom rather than making an absolute promise.

items.prompt: Translate into English: مع السلامة (ma‘a as-salāma)
items.answer: 'Go with safety/peace' — a farewell expression said to someone who is leaving.

items.prompt: A learner wrote: 'ما شاء الله (mā shā' Allāh) is used to say goodbye when someone leaves a party.' Identify the error and explain the correct meaning and usage.
items.answer: This is incorrect. ما شاء الله is an expression of admiration or praise (often to protect against the evil eye when complimenting someone), not a farewell. The correct farewell is مع السلامة (ma‘a as-salāma).

items.prompt: List three of the common expressions covered (with transliteration) and briefly state one context for each: greeting a guest, expressing gratitude for good health, and admiring something without jinxing it.
items.answer: أهلاً وسهلاً (ahlan wa sahlan) — greeting a guest; الحمد لله (al-ḥamdu lillāh) — expressing gratitude, e.g. for good health; ما شاء الله (mā shā' Allāh) — admiring something/someone while warding off envy or the evil eye.

items.prompt: Translate this proverb into English and explain its meaning in one sentence: الصبر مفتاح الفرج (as-sabru miftāḥu al-faraj)
items.answer: 'Patience is the key to relief/deliverance.' Meaning: enduring hardship patiently eventually leads to a solution or relief.

items.prompt: Complete the proverb with the missing word: من ___ يحصد (man ___ yaḥṣud) — 'He who sows, reaps.' Fill in the blank with the Arabic word for 'sows' (transliteration: yazra').
items.answer: يزرع (yazra')

items.prompt: The proverb الصبر مفتاح الفرج (as-sabru miftāḥu al-faraj) uses the noun صبر (ṣabr, 'patience'). Conjugate the verb صَبَرَ (ṣabara, 'he was patient') in the present tense (يفعل form) for: أنا (anā, I), أنتَ (anta, you m.), هي (hiya, she).
items.answer: أنا أصبر (anā aṣbir) - I am patient/endure; أنتَ تصبر (anta taṣbir) - you (m.) are patient; هي تصبر (hiya taṣbir) - she is patient

items.prompt: Find and correct the grammatical error in this rendering of the proverb 'The eye does not rise above the eyebrow': العين ما تعلو على الحاجب (al-'aynu mā ta'lā 'alā al-ḥājib). The learner wrote تعلو (ta'lū) as تعلا (ta'lā) by mistake — identify the correct verb form and explain why.
items.answer: The correct form is تعلو (ta'lū), not تعلا (ta'lā), because علا (ʿalā, 'to rise') is a defective verb ending in a weak letter that becomes و (wāw) in the present tense (تعلو) for feminine singular subjects like العين (al-'ayn), not ا (alif).

items.prompt: In your own words (English is fine), explain the practical life lesson behind the proverb القرد في عين أمه غزال (al-qirdu fī 'ayni ummihi ghazāl) — literally 'The monkey in his mother's eye is a gazelle.'
items.answer: It means that a mother (or anyone who loves someone) sees them as beautiful/perfect regardless of how they appear to others — love is blind to flaws, similar to the English idiom 'beauty is in the eye of the beholder.'

items.prompt: Translate this English proverb meaning into Arabic script with transliteration: 'Actions speak louder than words' — using the concept 'الأفعال أبلغ من الأقوال' (al-af'ālu ablaghu min al-aqwāl). Write it out and give a literal word-for-word gloss of الأفعال (al-af'āl) and الأقوال (al-aqwāl).
items.answer: الأفعال أبلغ من الأقوال (al-af'ālu ablaghu min al-aqwāl) — 'Actions are more eloquent than words.' الأفعال (al-af'āl) = 'the actions/deeds'; الأقوال (al-aqwāl) = 'the sayings/words'.

items.prompt: Complete the comparative structure in this proverb: الأفعال ___ من الأقوال (al-af'ālu ___ min al-aqwāl) meaning 'Actions are more eloquent than words.' Fill in the comparative adjective form (transliteration: ablaghu).
items.answer: أبلغ (ablaghu)

items.prompt: Write two full Arabic sentences (with transliteration) using the proverb الصبر مفتاح الفرج (as-sabru miftāḥu al-faraj) in a short original context, e.g., advising a friend who is struggling. Include an English translation of your sentences.
items.answer: Answers vary; example: يا صديقي، لا تقلق، الصبر مفتاح الفرج (yā ṣadīqī, lā taqlaq, aṣ-ṣabru miftāḥu al-faraj) - 'My friend, don't worry, patience is the key to relief.' أنا أعرف أن هذا صعب، لكن كل شيء سيتحسن (anā a'rifu anna hādhā ṣa'b, lākinna kulla shay'in sayataḥassan) - 'I know this is hard, but everything will improve.' Learner's sentences should correctly use the proverb in context.

items.prompt: Complete the proverb: الصبر ____ الفرج (as-sabru ____ al-faraj) — 'Patience is the ____ to relief.' Fill in the missing word (meaning 'key').
items.answer: مفتاح (miftah) — 'Patience is the key to relief.'

items.prompt: Translate this proverb into natural English: من جد وجد (man jadda wajad)
items.answer: Whoever strives (works hard) succeeds. (He who seeks, finds.)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic (write the proverb in Arabic script plus transliteration): 'Time is gold.'
items.answer: الوقت من ذهب (al-waqtu min dhahab)

items.prompt: The verb جدّ (jadda, 'to strive/work hard') is a past-tense verb in the proverb من جد وجد. Conjugate جدّ (jadda) in the past tense for أنتِ (anti, 'you' f.sg.) and هم (hum, 'they' m.pl.).
items.answer: أنتِ جددتِ (anti jadadti); هم جدّوا (hum jaddu)

items.prompt: This proverb has a wrong word. Find and correct it: العقل السليم في القلب السليم (al-'aqlu as-salimu fi al-qalbi as-salim) — 'A sound mind in a sound heart.'
items.answer: القلب (al-qalb, 'heart') should be الجسم (al-jism, 'body'): العقل السليم في الجسم السليم (al-'aqlu as-salimu fi al-jismi as-salim) — 'A sound mind in a sound body.'

items.prompt: Explain in one English sentence what this proverb means and give a situation where you'd use it: لا يلدغ المؤمن من جحر مرتين (la yuldaghu al-mu'minu min juhrin marratayn)
items.answer: It means a wise/faithful person doesn't make the same mistake twice (a believer isn't bitten from the same hole twice); used when someone learns from a past mistake and avoids repeating it.

items.prompt: Complete the proverb: كما ____ تدان (kama ____ tudan) — 'As you judge, so shall you be judged.' Fill in the missing verb (meaning 'you judge').
items.answer: تدين (tudin) — كما تدين تدان (kama tudinu tudan)

items.prompt: Translate into English: الجار قبل الدار (al-jaru qabla ad-dar)
items.answer: The neighbor (comes) before the house. (Choose your neighbor before you choose your house.)

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic (script + transliteration): 'Sometimes harm brings benefit.'
items.answer: رب ضارة نافعة (rubba dharratin nafi'ah)

items.prompt: This proverb has its two halves swapped. Correct it: في العجلة السلامة وفي التأني الندامة (fi al-'ajalati as-salamah wa fi at-ta'ani an-nadamah) — 'In haste is safety, in deliberation is regret.'
items.answer: Should be swapped: في التأني السلامة وفي العجلة الندامة (fi at-ta'ani as-salamah wa fi al-'ajalati an-nadamah) — 'In deliberation is safety, in haste is regret.'

items.prompt: Give the English equivalent proverb (with similar meaning) for: عصفور في اليد خير من عشرة على الشجرة (usfurun fil yad khayrun min 'asharatin 'ala ash-shajarah), and explain the literal meaning.
items.answer: Literal: 'A bird in the hand is better than ten on the tree.' English equivalent: 'A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.'

items.prompt: The verb أحسنت (ahsanta, 'you did good') comes from يُحسن (yuhsinu, 'to do good/be kind'). Conjugate يُحسن (yuhsinu) in the present tense for هي (hiya, 'she') and نحن (nahnu, 'we').
items.answer: هي تُحسن (hiya tuhsinu); نحن نُحسن (nahnu nuhsinu)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb كَتَبَ (kataba - 'he wrote') in the past tense for the pronoun أنتِ (anti - 'you, feminine singular'). Write the full Arabic form with transliteration.
items.answer: كَتَبْتِ (katabti) - 'you (f.) wrote'

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb يَذْهَبُ (yadhhabu - 'he goes/is going') in the present tense for the pronoun نَحْنُ (naḥnu - 'we'). Write the full Arabic form with transliteration.
items.answer: نَذْهَبُ (nadhhabu) - 'we go/are going'

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct present-tense form of شَرِبَ (shariba - 'to drink') for the subject هِيَ (hiya - 'she'): هِيَ ___ الْقَهْوَةَ (hiya ___ al-qahwata - 'She drinks the coffee').
items.answer: تَشْرَبُ (tashrabu)

items.prompt: Find and correct the conjugation error: أَنْتُم يَكْتُبُ الرِّسَالَةَ (antum yaktubu al-risālata) - intended meaning: 'You all write the letter.'
items.answer: Should be أَنْتُم تَكْتُبُونَ الرِّسَالَةَ (antum taktubūna al-risālata) - the verb must agree with the plural 'you' subject using the تَ- ...-ونَ (ta-...-ūna) pattern, not the يَ- (ya-) prefix used for 'he'.

items.prompt: Translate into Arabic (write the Arabic script with transliteration): 'They (masculine plural) study Arabic.'
items.answer: هُمْ يَدْرُسُونَ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ (hum yadrusūna al-‘arabiyyata)

items.prompt: When looking up the verb يَشْرَبُ (yashrabu - 'he drinks') in an Arabic-English mini-dictionary organized by root letters, which three root consonants would you search under? Write them in Arabic with transliteration.
items.answer: ش ر ب (sh-r-b), the root of شَرِبَ (shariba - 'to drink')

items.prompt: In an English-Arabic dictionary, you look up 'to open.' You find the entry: فَتَحَ (fataḥa) - 'he opened' (past tense, 3rd person masculine singular, the dictionary citation form). What present-tense form would you derive for 'she opens'? Write it with transliteration.
items.answer: تَفْتَحُ (taftaḥu) - 'she opens'

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct Arabic word after looking up 'book' in an English-Arabic mini-dictionary: قَرَأْتُ ___ (qara'tu ___) - 'I read the book.' (use the definite form)
items.answer: الْكِتَابَ (al-kitāba)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb كَتَبَ (kataba - to write) in the present tense (المضارع) for these pronouns: أنا (ana - I), أنتَ (anta - you, masc.), هي (hiya - she). Write each full form.
items.answer: أنا أكتُبُ (ana aktubu - I write); أنتَ تكتُبُ (anta taktubu - you write); هي تكتُبُ (hiya taktubu - she writes)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb ذَهَبَ (dhahaba - to go) in the past tense (الماضي) for: نحن (nahnu - we), أنتم (antum - you all, masc.), هم (hum - they, masc.).
items.answer: نحن ذَهَبْنا (nahnu dhahabnaa - we went); أنتم ذَهَبْتُم (antum dhahabtum - you all went); هم ذَهَبوا (hum dhahaboo - they went)

items.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct present-tense form of شَرِبَ (shariba - to drink) for 'هي' (hiya - she): هي ____ الماء (hiya ____ al-maa' - she drinks the water).
items.answer: تشرَبُ (tashrabu)

items.prompt: In a verb conjugation table, what does the root form usually listed at the top (like كَتَبَ kataba) represent grammatically, and which pronoun's past tense form is it identical to?
items.answer: It is the base/root form (3rd person masc. singular past tense, 'he'), identical to the هو (huwa - he) past tense form.

items.prompt: Find and correct the conjugation error: أنتِ يَكتُبُ الرسالة (anti yaktubu ar-risaala - you [fem.] write the letter).
items.answer: أنتِ تَكتُبينَ الرسالة (anti taktubeena ar-risaala)

items.prompt: Translate to Arabic: 'They (fem.) studied yesterday.'
items.answer: هُنَّ دَرَسْنَ بالأمس (hunna darasna bi-l-amsi)

items.prompt: When using an Arabic-English mini-dictionary, entries are typically alphabetized by the root letters, not the surface word. What is the root of the word مكتوب (maktoob - written) that you would search for?
items.answer: ك ت ب (k-t-b)

items.prompt: Using dictionary lookup skills, what English meaning would you expect to find under the root د ر س (d-r-s) in an Arabic-English dictionary?
items.answer: to study / lesson (related meanings like 'to learn, study, lesson')

items.prompt: Translate to English: أنا لا أفهمُ هذه الكلمة (ana laa afhamu hadhihi al-kalima).
items.answer: I do not understand this word.

items.prompt: You look up 'to eat' in an English-Arabic mini-dictionary and find أكَلَ (akala). Fill in the blank with the present-tense form for 'نحن' (nahnu - we): نحن ____ الطعام (nahnu ____ al-ta'aam - we eat the food).
items.answer: نأكُلُ (na'kulu)

items.prompt: Conjugate the verb فَهِمَ (fahima - to understand) in the present tense for: أنتما (antumaa - you two), هما (humaa - they two, masc.).
items.answer: أنتما تفهَمانِ (antumaa tafhamaani - you two understand); هما يفهَمانِ (humaa yafhamaani - they two understand)

items.prompt: In a verb conjugation table with columns for الماضي (al-maadi - past) and المضارع (al-mudaari' - present), which column would you check to find the correct form for 'سَتَذهَبُ' (sa-tadhhabu - she will go), and what element added to the present tense form creates the future meaning?
items.answer: You check the المضارع (present tense) column; adding the prefix سَـ (sa-) or the word سوف (sawfa) to the present tense form creates the future meaning.
